title: Kaveri: four regulators, one morning
debrief: Report what you know on time, then update. Don't hide a breach from the people it affects, and don't tell the press before the regulators and customers. One owner per clock.

k1.title: 05:10 UTC
k1.text: The CEO wants to wait until the developers are sure what happened before telling anyone outside.

choices.text: File CERT-In and RBI with what we know now, and update later
choices.note: Both clocks are six hours from noticing; partial facts are expected.

choices.text: Wait for the full root cause
choices.note: The root cause took until 07:15. Waiting risks missing the clock.

k2.title: 07:30 UTC
k2.text: The DPO asks who tells the customers, and when.

choices.text: Tell each affected customer without delay, in plain words, by SMS and email, with what they can do
choices.note: The DPDP Rules ask for each affected person to be told without delay.

choices.text: Tell customers only if the press finds out
choices.note: The duty doesn't depend on publicity.

k3.title: 08:20 UTC
k3.text: A journalist says she has a sample of the records.

choices.text: Confirm the incident briefly, say customers are being told, give no data
choices.note: Honest, short, and after the regulators and customers.
She has a sample. A denial becomes the story.

k4.title: 09:00 UTC
k4.text: 64 of the people affected live in Germany and Ireland.

choices.text: Check whether GDPR applies to Kaveri Remit, and if so notify the lead EU authority within 72 hours
choices.note: GDPR can apply to a company outside the EU that offers services to people in it.

choices.text: Ignore it: we are an Indian company
choices.note: Offering a service to EU residents can bring GDPR in.
